blocks.text: **The task.** Group a list of strings so that anagrams end up together. Two strings are anagrams if one is a rearrangement of the other.
Comparing every pair is O(N²). Instead, give each string a **signature** that is identical for anagrams and different for everything else — then group by signature with a map.
Sorting a word's letters is the obvious choice. `"eat"`, `"tea"` and `"ate"` all sort to `"aet"`.
Sorting each word costs O(K log K) for a word of length K. Counting letters is O(K):
The commas matter. Without a separator, counts of `[1, 11]` and `[11, 1]` would both become `"111"` and collide — a genuine bug, not a theoretical one.
This generalises well beyond anagrams. Whenever you need to group "things that are the same in some respect", define a signature capturing exactly that respect and use it as a map key.

items: Anagrams → sorted letters, or letter counts

blocks.text: **Time: O(N x K)** with counting signatures, or O(N x K log K) with sorting, for N words of length K.
**Space: O(N x K)** to hold the groups.
